rule: A convention is context, not an assignment. Domains still never pick a color. Each convention says how strong it is, how well it is evidenced, and how no-slop-color treats it: 'context' conventions are shown and represented by at most one direction; 'preferred' patterns rank higher because they are the tasteful default; 'cliche-risk' patterns stay available but are never boosted and are always flagged.

conventions.label: Blue as the lead color
conventions.summary: Blue is the most common lead color in finance logos, though red is close behind. Newer fintech brands depart from it more often.

evidence.claim: Blue leads finance logos at 31%, with red at 28%.

conventions.notes: No bank-specific share could be traced. A widely repeated '60–90% of banks use navy' figure was not found in any primary source and is not used.

conventions.label: Blue as the lead color
conventions.summary: Blue appears in a large share of technology logos.

evidence.claim: Blue appears in about 60% of tech logos, in an analysis of more than 14,000 logos.

conventions.notes: The figure covers technology broadly. Software sub-categories are recorded as soft because no separate figure was found.

conventions.label: Blue as the lead color
conventions.summary: Blue is reported as the dominant logo color in healthcare. Many wellness-leaning brands now avoid the clinical look.

evidence.claim: Blue was reported as the dominant logo color in healthcare, accounting, technology, real estate and marketing.

conventions.notes: The article could not be retrieved to confirm the figures. Claims such as '85% of healthcare logos are blue' are not used.

conventions.label: Black, or black and white
conventions.summary: The most tasteful luxury language is black, or black and white: severe, restrained and exclusive without a metallic cue.

evidence.claim: Owner's taste rule (2026-11-10): for luxury, prefer black or black-and-white directions. Gold is present in the category but is the easier cliché.

conventions.notes: Recorded as curation, not as a measured frequency. No quantified luxury logo study was found.

conventions.label: Gold on black
conventions.summary: Gold signals premium conventionally and is easy to execute poorly. Keep it scarce and flat when used.

evidence.claim: Owner's taste rule (2026-11-10): black and gold is closer to conventional premium signalling than to current high-taste luxury.

conventions.notes: Never boosted. Shown only when the query selects it on other grounds or the user asks to follow conventions.

unverified.claim: Red is the dominant color in food and beverage.
unverified.reason: Commonly repeated, often with appetite-psychology claims this project does not make. No measured source checked yet.
